answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a scarce-slot auction mechanism where identities compete for limited access. Each new identity must win a slot, starting the bidding at 10 tokens and increasing the price by 5 tokens for each additional participant. If 10 fake identities are created, costs can escalate to over 100 tokens, forcing attackers to face substantial financial risks. In this way, each additional entrant transforms the bidding dynamic, reminiscent of trudging up a shifting dune, with every ripple in cost whispering warnings of a looming financial collapse.
